doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Roy Eldridge in Pittsburgh in 1925
summary: Carter played once or twice with Roy and Joe Eldridge's Pittsburgh band and admired Roy's originality.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: One more artist who we just mentioned in passing, but maybe you can elaborate on a bit more, is Roy Eldridge.

Oh, Roy, I played with Roy in 1925. He and his brother Joe had an orchestra in Pittsburgh called the Elyte [phonetic] or Elite Serenaders. I had occasion to play with them once or twice. But he was an original.

Oh, even then, yeah. Even though he patterned himself pretty much after Armstrong and then went on after that, from that, and as everybody says, the tree then . . . the next branch was [Dizzy] Gillespie and so on. But, oh, I had a great admiration for Roy Eldridge, as everyone did.
